issues.body:
The /sparql section states flatly: "The endpoint assembles one named graph per RDF resource that the caller may read under WAC. The default graph is empty."

That is true by default, but the implementation ships a documented reserved opt-in that the skill never mentions: src/sparql_endpoint.rs:28-29 defines UNION_DEFAULT_GRAPH_IRI = "http://www.w3.org/ns/solid/sparql#union-default-graph", and expand_union_default() (src/sparql_endpoint.rs:214+) rewrites that IRI in the query dataset's default position into the full set of authorized graph names. It is exercised by the integration test protocol_get_form_post_construct_and_union_default_are_live (tests/sparql_endpoint.rs:259), so it is a live, tested surface.

Impact is usability, not correctness: an agent or operator following this skill writes SELECT ... WHERE { ?s ?p ?o }, gets zero results, and has nothing in the doc explaining why or how to fix it. The skill's own example works around this by using GRAPH ?g { ?s ?p ?o }, which masks the gap rather than closing it. Since a SKILL.md is the agent-facing usage surface for this server, the one documented escape hatch for the empty default graph belongs in it.

The security envelope is unaffected: the expansion draws only from authorized.graph_names, so the opt-in cannot widen visibility beyond what WAC already allowed.
issues.fix_hint: In the "Query readable RDF with /sparql" section, after "The default graph is empty.", add roughly: "Pass default-graph-uri=http://www.w3.org/ns/solid/sparql#union-default-graph to expand the default graph to the union of the graphs the caller is authorized to read; the expansion draws only from that authorized set, so it cannot widen visibility." A one-line curl variant of the existing example would make it copy-pasteable.
issues.title: Omits the union-default-graph opt-in, so "The default graph is empty" leaves the reader no way to query across all readable resources

issues.body:
The skill says "The default `sparql-endpoint` feature exposes authenticated `GET` and `POST` SPARQL Protocol query operations" and every /sparql example carries Authorization + DPoP headers. A reader reasonably concludes /sparql is closed to unauthenticated callers.

It is not. auth_middleware distinguishes an ABSENT Authorization header from a malformed one and treats absent as a valid public identity rather than a 401 (src/auth.rs:471, and the rationale at src/auth.rs:377: "an anonymous request is a valid, public identity"). /sparql is mounted behind that same middleware (src/app.rs:334-348), so an anonymous request reaches the handler with a public VerifiedToken and receives every publicly-readable resource as a named graph.

This is not a vulnerability — dataset assembly is the security boundary and it runs the same per-resource WAC read decision as LDP GET, so an anonymous caller gets exactly the public slice they could already fetch resource-by-resource. But it is an operationally meaningful difference: /sparql lets an anonymous caller enumerate and join across all public resources in a single request, which is a materially different exposure profile from per-resource GETs, and an operator sizing their public posture should see it stated. The doc already correctly notes elsewhere that public reads bypass the auth path; that note just is not connected to the /sparql surface.
issues.fix_hint: Rephrase to "exposes `GET` and `POST` SPARQL Protocol query operations" and add a sentence to the same section: "An unauthenticated request is treated as the public identity and receives only publicly-readable resources; supply Authorization + DPoP to query the resources your WebID is authorized to read." Consider a matching note under "Operational checks and boundaries" that this enables single-request enumeration of the public slice.
issues.title: "exposes authenticated GET and POST" understates that /sparql also serves anonymous callers the public-readable slice

verdict.summary:
Doc-only PR: adds skills/solid-lws-server/SKILL.md and registers it in the skills/SKILL.md index. No source changes, so review reduces to whether each documented claim traces to real sparq-lws-core behavior. I verified them against source.

Verified accurate: default bind 127.0.0.1:3000 / base URL http://localhost:3000 (main.rs:313-314); SOLID_SERVER_AUDIENCE defaults to base_url (main.rs:318); default features [embedded-sparq, sparql-endpoint], --no-default-features gives the engine-free tier with /sparql compiled out (Cargo.toml, app.rs:334); PSS_SPARQ_BACKEND memory|embedded|http, memory the boot default, http behind --features http-sparq; setting only one of TLS_CERT/TLS_KEY fails startup (tls.rs:327-355); seed flags refused on non-memory backends absent ALLOW_SEED_NONMEMORY (main.rs:286-288, 698); BIDIRECTIONAL strict|warn|off; /livez+/readyz unauthenticated (app.rs:430-439); redis-replay opt-in; unknown Accept degrades to text/turtle while explicit q=0 is 406 (content.rs:15, 485, tests 584/598); Range 206/416; Slug is a non-binding prefix with a collision-independent minted Location (handler.rs:2197-2214), matching the doc's "use the returned Location"; /sparql supports SELECT/ASK/CONSTRUCT and rejects DESCRIBE + Update (sparql_endpoint.rs:130-176). The in-memory-blob caveat is correct (all three backend arms build InMemoryBlobStore). The JSON-LD "local, context-free compaction, not the W3C Compaction Algorithm" caveat matches content.rs:157-213 and is a genuine anti-overclaim. Framing ("experimental", "does not replace the TypeScript prod-solid-server") matches the crate README. All five cross-referenced SKILL.md paths and the crate README exist.

Gates: check-terminology.py and check-privacy-claims.sh clean, no hard-coded perf numbers, the frontmatter description is quoted so its colon cannot break the YAML render gate, name matches the directory.

Two minor completeness nits below; neither is a correctness or security defect, so this approves.
